chains.title: FOXA1 gain-of-binding at the alt allele activates TOX3

links.claim: FOXA1 binds the alt A allele more strongly than the ref G allele at rs56007086; this is a literature/context-based hypothesis, and no QBiC-SELEX model or ChIP occupancy evidence is supplied in this case.
rs56007086 lies in a 16q12 element near TOX3 that is plausibly an enhancer in breast-cancer cells.
The enhancer regulates TOX3.
FOXA1 is expressed and active in MCF7 breast cancer cells.
Increased TOX3 enhancer activity and TOX3 expression promote breast-cancer risk.

predictions: Alt A increases enhancer activity and TOX3 expression in MCF7.
The risk/effect allele tracks with higher TOX3 expression.
falsified_if: Allele-specific FOXA1 ChIP or EMSA shows no differential FOXA1 binding between G and A.
Editing G>A in MCF7 does not alter TOX3 expression or enhancer activity.

chains.title: No TF-mediated allelic effect; linked causal variant or null
predictions: No allele-specific TF occupancy at rs56007086.
The association is explained by LD with a nearby causal variant or by chance/passenger effects.
Editing rs56007086 alone does not change TOX3 expression.
falsified_if: Fine-mapping and functional assays show rs56007086 itself has allele-specific TF binding and regulatory activity.
No linked causal variant can explain the association.

chains.title: GATA3 loss-of-binding at the alt allele derepresses TOX3

links.claim: GATA3 binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt A allele at rs56007086; no QBiC-SELEX model or occupancy evidence is supplied, so this is a competing motif hypothesis.
The variant sits in a TOX3-associated 16q12 regulatory element.
GATA3 occupancy at this element represses TOX3.
GATA3 is a key breast epithelial TF expressed in MCF7 cells.
Loss of GATA3 repression increases TOX3 and breast-cancer risk.

predictions: Ref G increases GATA3 occupancy relative to alt A.
Alt A reduces GATA3-dependent repression and increases TOX3 expression.
GATA3 knockdown should mimic the alt allele.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP or EMSA shows no preferential GATA3 binding to G over A.
GATA3 knockdown does not change TOX3 expression or enhancer activity.

chains.title: CEBPB gain-of-binding at the alt allele activates TOX3

links.claim: CEBPB binds the alt A allele more strongly than the ref G allele; no QBiC-SELEX model or occupancy evidence is supplied, so this is a lower-confidence motif hypothesis.
The variant is in a candidate 16q12 enhancer near TOX3.
CEBPB binding activates TOX3.
CEBPB is expressed in MCF7 breast cancer cells.
Higher TOX3 contributes to breast-cancer risk.

predictions: CEBPB knockdown reduces the alt-allele enhancer effect.
falsified_if: CEBPB ChIP or EMSA shows no allele-specific binding at rs56007086.
CEBPB perturbation does not affect TOX3 or the enhancer.

chains.title: ZNF263 loss-of-binding at the alt allele derepresses TOX3

links.claim: ZNF263 binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt A allele; no QBiC-SELEX model or occupancy evidence is supplied, so this is a low-confidence motif hypothesis.
The variant lies in a 16q12 element near TOX3.
ZNF263 represses TOX3.
ZNF263 is expressed in MCF7 cells.
Loss of ZNF263 repression increases TOX3 and breast-cancer risk.

predictions: Alt A reduces ZNF263 binding and increases TOX3.
falsified_if: ZNF263 ChIP or EMSA shows no allele-specific binding.
ZNF263 perturbation does not alter TOX3 expression.

matrix.test: Recombinant EMSA with FOXA1 and GATA3 on ref-G and alt-A probes, including competition and supershift controls.

outcomes.outcome: Alt A probe shifts with FOXA1; ref G does not.
Ref G probe shifts with GATA3; alt A does not.

next_experiment: Perform recombinant EMSA with FOXA1 and GATA3 on ref-G and alt-A probes; this is the cheapest single experiment that can distinguish the top two chains because they differ in both TF identity (FOXA1 vs GATA3) and preferred allele (alt vs ref).
